name: Energy, utilities and land-based operations
one_line: The operator-side record of obtaining, growing, generating, transmitting or metering a physical resource at a licensed source or operating site: permits and tenements, wells and fields, mines and quarries, farms and forests, fisheries, generation assets, grid or utility meters, production and yield returns, source-to-volume reconciliations, and environmental monitoring tied to the authorised activity. Its anchor is a relation among an operating source/site, an authority or tenure, an asset or production unit, and measured output or environmental performance over a stated period. It is not manufacturing merely because material is produced, engineering merely because plant is designed, logistics merely because output moves, construction merely because land is involved, or government merely because a permit exists. Placeholder schema row (J-IND, full J-DEPTH): PR-6 keeps fields empty; the proposed field set is for R1c adjudication only.

node_test.why: The schema survives because the smallest useful grammar is source_or_site + operating_authority + asset + output_stream + reporting_period + record_type. The distinctive join is authorised source-to-measured-output: a permit or tenement defines where and under what right an activity occurs; operating records tie a well, pit, field, compartment, vessel, generator, feeder or meter to quantities and environmental observations for a period. Manufacturing instead keys recurring transformation to product/batch/lot and quality event; engineering keys controlled technical definition to design item and lifecycle; logistics keys custody and movement; construction_property keys a property/site to a professional instruction; government owns issuer-side licensing and regulatory case administration. None of those defaults can express an operator reconciling authorised source, operating unit and measured output without semantic distortion. Quantities themselves remain content/search evidence and are not proposed as folder dimensions.

proposed_fields.example: North Quarry / Solar Farm A / Field 12
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: REUSE the exact `site` key already proposed by manufacturing; do not mint a resource-specific synonym. `location` is the Photos capture-location role, while this is the operating place a record is about. One environmental sample may be captured downstream while documenting North Quarry, so the roles cannot be collapsed. R1c should adjudicate `site` once for both operational schemas.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE for a genuinely multi-site corpus; otherwise flatten the one-child level. A site makes an asset, permit and output stream intelligible and is not authorship.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Site, Field, Lease, Mine, Farm, Forest Unit, Facility or Supply Area slot can be direct evidence. An address, coordinate or place name in prose remains possible because it may be a regulator office, customer, delivery point, monitoring station or cited location.

proposed_fields.example: Mining Lease ML-2048 / Water Abstraction Permit WA-73
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No canonical key identifies the right, tenure, licence, concession, quota or connection agreement under which the holder operates at a source. `institution` is a financial issuer; `purpose` belongs to applications; `project` is bounded work; `property` is a construction proposal. Government may hold the same identifier in its issuer-side case, but this key represents the operator's enduring authority and its conditions, not the issuing agency.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE only where one operator manages several authorities or tenements. It may sit beneath site; it must be flattened where it creates a single child or exposes a sensitive concession identifier unnecessarily.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires an identifier in a labelled Permit, Licence, Lease, Tenement, Concession, Quota or Connection Agreement slot plus an issuing-body/holder/effective-area structure. R2/R4 own identifier patterns and authority gazetteers; this row defines neither.

proposed_fields.example: Well BR-17 / Turbine WT-04 / Meter MPAN …7812
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: REUSE the exact `asset` key already proposed by manufacturing. It names the enduring controlled operating unit that produces, conveys or measures output. `camera_information` is capture equipment; `repository` is code; `project` is work. Resource operations adds evidence that the same key must cover wells, pits, compartments, generators, feeders, pumps and meters without becoming a private synonym.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE in asset-led branches, where the asset makes a meter read, production return, maintenance record or monitoring series intelligible. It is optional beneath site and should not be forced into area-led farming or forestry records.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation needs an asset identifier in a labelled Well, Pit, Turbine, Generator, Feeder, Meter, Pump, Vessel or Compartment slot, preferably cross-checked against a local asset register. A serial-like token alone is never sufficient.

proposed_fields.example: raw water abstraction / saleable ore / electricity exported / wheat harvest
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No canonical key names what physical resource or metered service the operation produces, extracts, grows, lands, generates or supplies. Manufacturing's proposed `product` is close but implies an article or formulation made through transformation; crude production, standing timber, catch, abstraction, generation and metered utility service are not all products without erasing the source relation. R1c may widen `product` to a neutral output key, but must not retain both as synonyms if one global role works.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE as the subject below site/authority when one operation has materially different output streams. A quantity or unit is never part of the folder value.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Direct only from a labelled Commodity, Crop, Species, Product Stream, Fuel, Service or Export Register slot. Free prose and filenames remain possible because the same resource name appears in forecasts, engineering specifications, invoices and cited reports.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No canonical key expresses the period the measured operation is ABOUT. `creation_date` is when bytes were created, `tax_year` is statutory finance, `term` is academic, `capture_year` is photos, and business_operations proposes `fiscal_period` for management cycles. This key covers daily production, monthly regulatory returns, crop years and metering intervals. R1c should consider a globally neutral period key rather than proliferating period synonyms.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE only after site/output or asset and normally as an optional leaf. It is never time-first because year-first scatters the same operating source across calendar branches.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a date or interval in a labelled Reporting Period, Production Date, Crop Year, Billing Period or Settlement Interval slot with an operational-measure context. A filename year or filesystem timestamp remains possible.

proposed_fields.example: production return / meter-read export / environmental monitoring report
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: REUSE the canonical Finance key rather than minting `resource_record_type`. R1c must decide whether `record_type` is intentionally global; if its finance role is binding, the solution is one global document-function key, not another private spelling.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Inherited from the canonical row if widened/reused; it is the leaf below the operating subject and period.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled form title and its supporting structure may establish a value. Extension, filename and isolated type words do not.

template.why: Empty by the placeholder contract because this schema declares no field rows. Subject to R1c, the researched default is site → operating_authority → output_stream → reporting_period → record_type, with an asset-led alternative site → asset → record_type for utilities, generation and integrity work. It is not time-first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Quantities, units, coordinates, permit conditions and environmental results remain content/search evidence, never folder levels. The user may reverse, remove, add or flatten dimensions after facts are validated.

collides_with.signal: Both hold asset maintenance, environmental compliance and quantities. Manufacturing wins when product/batch/lot transformation or quality-event structure is central; resource_operations wins when an authorised natural/utility source and measured extraction, generation, harvest, landing, supply or environmental condition is central. Same fixture: WT-04_Gearbox-Replacement-Work-Order.pdf is manufacturing unless joined to an accepted operating-output series.

Both hold plant drawings, calculations and commissioning evidence. Engineering wins on controlled design item, revision/baseline and requirement verification; resource_operations wins on the operating source/authority and measured-period record. Same fixture: North-Quarry-Plant-Layout_RevC.dwg remains engineering.

Both hold commodity movements, vessels, storage and quantities. Logistics wins on consignment/custody/origin-destination movement; resource_operations wins on source-to-output reconciliation under an operating authority. Same fixture: June-Ore-Shipments.csv remains logistics.

Both hold sites, land access, permits, surveys and handover records. Construction_property wins when property/site is joined to a bounded professional instruction or works contract; resource_operations wins after operation begins and authority/source/output recur. A grid-connection construction pack stays construction until operational meter/dispatch series exists.

Both can hold the same permit and environmental return. Government wins for issuer-side application, review, inspection, enforcement and public administration; resource_operations wins for the holder/operator's authority, production and compliance series. Same bytes may be legal in both schemas, so issuer/holder role must be cited rather than inferred from letterhead.

Both hold budgets, audits, contracts, policies and project plans. Business operations wins for entity governance and generic delivery; resource_operations requires the source/site-authority-asset/output relation. A sustainability strategy with no measured site series is business_operations.

roles: government = issuer-side licensing, surveillance or enforcement case
photos.location/camera_information = where and how the image was captured

sensitivity_why: Production rates, reserves, meter identifiers, coordinates, critical-infrastructure layouts, environmental exceedances, land rights and farm/vessel locations can be commercially sensitive, security-relevant or identifying. The row assigns no handling class and does not make raw quantities, coordinates or conditions destination dimensions.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-RESOURCE-1: should R1c license a shared operational core (`site`, `asset`, neutral output/product, neutral reporting period, global `record_type`) across manufacturing and resource_operations, with only `operating_authority` distinct, or preserve two schemas because authorised-source-to-output recognition and privacy differ materially? NJ-RESOURCE-2: should a permit/tenement identifier ever be destination-eligible by default, given retrieval value versus disclosure of concession and infrastructure identifiers?
